description: This student study for the University of British Columbia's SEEDS Sustainability Program assesses whether sea water heat pumps could decarbonise the campus district energy system, which after replacing its steam plant relies on natural gas boilers, a biomass plant, a planned biomass expansion and cogeneration. Written by Thivya Viswanathan, it integrates each of four sea water heat pump technologies into a business-as-usual model and compares energy use, operating costs and greenhouse gas emissions from 2024 to 2050, with payback periods and other financial measures under several carbon tax scenarios. Coverage is the UBC Vancouver campus district energy system. The report is accessible online as a PDF in UBC Library Open Collections at no cost, with no licence stated on the record. Caveats: the report carries a SEEDS disclaimer that it is a student project, not an official UBC document, and may not reflect current activities. It shows investment appraisal of heat pumps for a campus heat network, with simulation uses in capacity planning. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
